definitions.explanation: A tall, large-flowered iris with sword-shaped leaves, planted in damp gardens and along stream banks. Blooms June through early July in a wide range of cultivated colors.

examples.japanese: {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}を{植|う}えた。
{花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}は{梅雨|つゆ}の{時期|じき}に{見頃|みごろ}を{迎|むか}える。
examples.english: Japanese irises reach their peak during the rainy season.

examples.japanese: {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}には{江戸|えど}{系|けい}・{伊勢|いせ}{系|けい}・{肥後|ひご}{系|けい}など、{産地|さんち}ごとに{特徴|とくちょう}のある{品種群|ひんしゅぐん}がある。
examples.english: Japanese irises come in regional cultivar groups — Edo, Ise, Higo — each with its own characteristics.

notes:
Often confused with アヤメ and {杜若|かきつばた} (rabbitear iris). The dividing rule of thumb: {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ} is the tallest and is grown on damp land, {杜若|かきつばた} grows in shallow water, and アヤメ prefers drier soil.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {杜若|かきつばた}: rabbitear iris — water-grown; smaller; blooms slightly earlier
- アヤメ: Siberian iris — drier soil; smaller flowers
- {菖蒲|しょうぶ}: sweet flag — different plant entirely; the iris is the "{花|はな}" (flowering) version of the name only

In the iris-festival custom on {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day, May 5), it is the leaves of {菖蒲|しょうぶ} (sweet flag), not {花菖蒲|はなしょうぶ}, that are used in the bath.
